                    ### Question
                    A 55-year-old Caucasian male presents for a routine colonoscopy. A polyp is found in the patient's transverse colon and is found to be cancerous on histological evaluation. Upon examination, it is found that these cancerous cells have decreased MHC class I expression on their surface. Which immune system cell is most capable of killing these tumor cells?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Natural killer cells
opb. B-cells
opc. Macrophages
opd. Eosinophils
ope. Cytotoxic T-cells

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Natural killer (NK) cells are the most capable immune cells for killing tumor cells with decreased MHC class I expression. This is because NK cells are uniquely equipped to recognize and eliminate cells that have downregulated MHC class I molecules, a common mechanism by which tumor cells evade cytotoxic T-cell mediated destruction. The reasoning chains for NK cells accurately reflect this mechanism, supported by evidence paths showing interactions between NK cells and unspecified tumor cells. Other immune cells like B-cells, macrophages, eosinophils, and even cytotoxic T-cells are less effective in this specific context due to their reliance on higher or normal levels of MHC class I expression for optimal function. The evidence paths confirm the specialized interaction between NK cells and tumor cells, reinforcing their role in targeting cells with abnormal MHC class I expression.
